Each branch must act in complete isolation, with no shared functions at all as the record shows.

Option B ("Any check by one branch on another is a violation of separation of powers for this case") is wrong because it confuses checks with usurpation. Option D ("Each branch must act in complete isolation, with no shared functions at all as the record shows") is wrong because it assumes powers never overlap.
